facts.meaning: In C, '=' assigns a value; '==' compares values for equality.
Integer division truncates toward zero; convert an operand to floating point before dividing to retain a fractional result.
semanticChecks: Both integer operands and truncation toward zero must remain explicit.
Conversion must occur before division, not only after the fraction has been discarded.

facts.meaning: A C string ends with the null character '\0'; strlen counts preceding bytes and excludes that terminator.
semanticChecks: The string terminator is a null character, not a null pointer.
strlen returns byte length before the terminator; do not claim a general Unicode character count.

facts.meaning: Returning a result passes it to the caller; printing displays it and is a distinct operation.
semanticChecks: Distinguish displaying a value from returning that value.
Do not infer that printf itself has no return value.

facts.meaning: Linear search can inspect an unsorted array one element at a time; its worst-case running time is O(n).
patterns: 线性查找.{0,100}(?:不需要有序|无需排序|未排序|无序).{0,100}O\s*\(\s*n\s*\)
semanticChecks: O(n) describes worst-case work here, not a claim that every search visits every element.

facts.meaning: Binary search halves the candidate region of a sorted array and takes O(log n) comparisons in the worst case.
semanticChecks: The sorted-order precondition and repeated halving must both remain.
Time complexity assumes constant-time access to array elements; do not generalize to arbitrary linked-list access.

facts.meaning: Selection sort repeatedly selects the remaining minimum; its running time is O(n^2), including already sorted input.
semanticChecks: Retain the repeated minimum selection and quadratic work.
Do not give selection sort a linear best case merely because the input is already sorted.

facts.meaning: Merge sort recursively sorts smaller parts and merges their sorted results; its usual array implementation has worst-case O(n log n) running time.
A pointer stores an address; '&' obtains an object's address and '*' dereferences a valid pointer to access the object.
semanticChecks: Keep address storage distinct from the pointed-to value.
Dereferencing requires a valid pointer to an appropriate live object.

facts.meaning: Pointer assignment copies an address, not the pointed-to data; aliases may observe changes to the same underlying memory.
semanticChecks: Do not imply that assigning a pointer creates an independent copy of its data.

facts.meaning: malloc may return NULL on failure; check the returned pointer before accessing allocated storage.
semanticChecks: Do not assume malloc always succeeds.
NULL is a pointer failure result here, distinct from a string's null terminator.

facts.meaning: Free an allocation once after its last use; do not access it through old pointers or aliases or free it again.
semanticChecks: The allocation's lifetime ends for aliases too.
Do not infer that free sets all aliases to NULL or prevents later invalid accesses automatically.
